key_insight: Structure-preserving Fourier quantum circuits can simulate wave-equation dynamics on a trapped-ion processor while preserving physically meaningful observables, even for large encoded grids.
engineering_relevance: This shows that near-term quantum hardware can resolve useful subdomain energy dynamics for structured PDEs with thousands of encoded degrees of freedom, suggesting a path toward scalable quantum scientific computing.
method: Fourier-based, structure-preserving circuits for 1D and 2D acoustic wave equations and Dirac dynamics with variable mass.
Encode wave fields on grids up to 1024 points in 1D and 32×32 in 2D, then estimate subdomain kinetic energies directly from measurement samples.
Benchmark compiled circuits on the Quantinuum H2-2 trapped-ion processor with fixed bandwidth and product-formula time stepping.
evidence_signal: Across all tested problems, measured kinetic-energy dynamics matched classical references with mean absolute errors of 5.9×10^-3 to 2.4×10^-2.
watch_item: Compilation cost grows approximately quadratically with the number of grid qubits, and the Dirac case also incurs extra cost as the number of product-formula steps increases.
paper_title: Structure-Preserving Quantum Simulation of Wave Equations on a Trapped-Ion Processor
